display_decisions_supported: Show a still poster of the first frame first; never autoplay.
Play the animation only on an explicit visitor request after a flashing warning; poster only under prefers-reduced-motion.
Show the animation no larger than 768 CSS pixels (15.3 percent at 768 px; 24.3 percent at the 200 percent zoom equivalent of 1,536 px).
No enlarged, zoomed, or full-screen animation until an independent flash review confirms or revises these limits.
limitations: This is the Museum's computation under the WCAG 2.2 definitions, not a certified photosensitive-epilepsy test, and it has not yet been independently reviewed.
Display size is modelled on a 1024 x 768 reference screen; physical screen size, viewing distance, and browser scaling are not measured.
The method files are retained as text with a .txt suffix so that they are evidence, not repository tooling.

method.definitions: WCAG 2.2 general flash and red flash, as stated in flash-analysis.json method
method.one_second_window: 20 frame intervals (21 states) evaluated at every loop phase; max taken
method.reproduction: Re-running both scripts on the retained GIF reproduced flash-analysis.json, the three masks, and flash-windows-presentation-widths.json byte for byte on 2026-10-18.

scripts.analysis: method/flash.py.txt (run as flash.py with method/gif_structure.py.txt beside it as gif_structure.py): python -I flash.py <gif> <out dir>
scripts.presentation_widths: method/flash_windows.py.txt (run as flash_windows.py beside flash.py): python -I flash_windows.py <dir holding the two raw/flash-concurrent-*-1000.png masks>

method.ten_degree_field: 341 x 256 px on a 1024 x 768 reference screen; for images larger than 1,000 px the window is scaled onto a 1,000 px coverage grid

results.wcag_2_3_1: general-flash area below the 25 percent limit up to 1,536 px (24.3 percent, narrowly) and above it from 2,048 px (30.2 percent); red flashes stay far below the limit
results.wcag_2_3_2: not met at any size: about 5.5 percent of the image flashes more than three times a second

source.decoding: exact palette indices of all eight frames decoded by the retained stdlib GIF decoder (method/gif_structure.py.txt)
